title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Adopted judgment: complaint denied; the SJC answered “No” to whether Tennessee Valley Presbytery erred in approving Redeemer Church’s session minutes without exception and in denying the complaint. The SJC’s stated basis was that Presbytery adopted no grounds for its actions and the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in interpreting the Constitution; it did not rule on whether a Super Bowl party violates the Sabbath. Separate concurrence by TE Sartorius emphasized that limit; separate dissent by RE Eggert would have held the complaint judicially out of order for lack of SJC jurisdiction over a presbytery’s BCO 40 review of session records. Vote: 18-1, four absent, one recused.
first_summary: Biese and others complained that Tennessee Valley Presbytery wrongly approved Redeemer Church’s session minutes without exception for a youth Super Bowl party and then denied their complaint. The SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find error. A concurrence and dissent were filed.
summary: Biese and others complained that Tennessee Valley Presbytery erred by approving Redeemer Church session minutes without exception—minutes noting a youth Super Bowl party—and by denying their complaint seeking a Sabbath exception. The SJC denied the complaint: because Presbytery gave no reasons for its actions, the record was insufficient to find it erred in interpreting the Constitution. A concurrence said the denial did not decide the Sabbath merits; a dissent would have held the complaint judicially out of order for lack of SJC jurisdiction over presbytery record review.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case No. 2023-04, Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery, SJC decision on complaint, 51st GA (2024), source lines 13–17. Adopted by the SJC 18-1, with four absent and one recused, after a 3-0 panel vote; source lines 72–76.
evidence_notes.dispute: Complainants challenged Tennessee Valley Presbytery’s October 2022 approval without exception of Redeemer Church session minutes containing “The youth group will have an outdoor Super Bowl Party on Feb. 7,” and its later denial of their complaint; source lines 21–29, 47–49, 131–133.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC answered “No” and denied the complaint because Presbytery adopted no grounds and the record was insufficient to find constitutional error; source lines 39–43, 53–65. The concurrence disclaimed any Sabbath-merits holding; source lines 84–121. The dissent would have held the complaint judicially out of order for lack of SJC jurisdiction over presbytery session-record review, except BCO 40-5 matters; source lines 139–481.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The concurrence and dissent are separate opinions, not the adopted judgment. Vote and recusal details appear at source lines 72–76. The source contains inconsistent dates—facts line 21 says Jan. 26, 2022 and meeting 10/18/22, while reasoning line 47 says Jan. 26, 2021 and Oct. 8, 2022; the synopsis avoids choosing among inconsistent exact dates.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. The decision does not incorporate another decision by reference; the concurrence and dissent are separate opinions, not incorporated results.

source_limits: The source supplies the SJC decision plus concurring and dissenting opinions, but not the underlying Redeemer session minutes, Tennessee Valley Presbytery minutes, or review committee report. The adopted decision itself states the record was insufficient. Internal date conflicts appear in the source (lines 21, 23, 39, 47, 131); the synopsis therefore avoids inconsistent exact dates.
benchmark_examples: C01 (1978-02 Allin): preserve procedural and substantive outcomes distinctly; here the adopted denial and its record-insufficiency reason must be separated from the concurrence and dissent.
C20 (2016-13 Daniels): do not supply a missing rationale; here the SJC did explain its denial as record insufficiency, while the dissent’s jurisdictional theory remains non-adopted.
